t: Beguin draws first-ever chemical equation
c: 1615 – Jean Beguin publishes the Tyrocinium Chymicum, an early chemistry textbook, and in it draws the first-ever chemical equation.

t: Descartes outlines scientific method
c: 1637 – René Descartes publishes Discours de la méthode, which contains an outline of the scientific method.

t: Van Helmont's Ortus medicinae establishes mass conservation
c: 1648 – Posthumous publication of the book Ortus medicinae by Jan Baptist van Helmont, which is cited by some as a major transitional work between alchemy and…

t: Boyle proposes law of gas pressure-volume
c: 1662 – Robert Boyle proposes Boyle's law, an experimentally based description of the behavior of gases, specifically the relationship between pressure and…

t: Brandt discovers cobalt element
c: 1735 – Swedish chemist Georg Brandt analyzes a dark blue pigment found in copper ore.

t: Black isolates carbon dioxide
c: 1754 – Joseph Black isolates carbon dioxide, which he called "fixed air".

t: Cadet creates first synthetic organometallic compound

t: Black formulates latent heat concept
c: 1758 – Joseph Black formulates the concept of latent heat to explain the thermochemistry of phase changes.

t: Cavendish discovers hydrogen gas
c: 1766 – Henry Cavendish discovers hydrogen as a colorless, odourless gas that burns and can form an explosive mixture with air.

t: Scheele and Priestley independently isolate oxygen
c: 1773–1774 – Carl Wilhelm Scheele and Joseph Priestley independently isolate oxygen, called by Priestley "dephlogisticated air" and Scheele "fire air".

t: Lavoisier names oxygen and explains combustion
c: 1778 – Antoine Lavoisier, considered "The father of modern chemistry", recognizes and names oxygen, and recognizes its importance and role in combustion.

t: Lavoisier publishes modern chemical nomenclature system
c: 1787 – Antoine Lavoisier publishes Méthode de nomenclature chimique, the first modern system of chemical nomenclature.

t: Charles proposes gas temperature-volume law
c: 1787 – Jacques Charles proposes Charles's law, a corollary of Boyle's law, describes relationship between temperature and volume of a gas.

t: Proust proposes law of definite proportions
c: 1797 – Joseph Proust proposes the law of definite proportions, which states that elements always combine in small, whole number ratios to form compounds.

t: Volta devises first chemical battery
c: 1800 – Alessandro Volta devises the first chemical battery, thereby founding the discipline of electrochemistry.

t: Dalton proposes gas mixture pressure law
c: 1803 – John Dalton proposes Dalton's law, which describes relationship between the components in a mixture of gases and the relative pressure each contributes…

t: Gay-Lussac discovers water hydrogen-oxygen ratio
c: 1805 – Joseph Louis Gay-Lussac discovers that water is composed of two parts hydrogen and one part oxygen by volume.

t: Gay-Lussac studies gas properties and laws
c: 1808 – Joseph Louis Gay-Lussac collects and discovers several chemical and physical properties of air and of other gases, including experimental proofs of…

t: Dalton publishes atomic theory and multiple proportions

t: Berzelius proposes chemical symbols and atomic weights
c: 1808 – Jöns Jakob Berzelius publishes Lärbok i Kemien in which he proposes modern chemical symbols and notation, and of the concept of relative atomic weight.

t: Avogadro proposes Avogadro's law for gases
c: 1811 – Amedeo Avogadro proposes Avogadro's law, that equal volumes of gases under constant temperature and pressure contain equal number of molecules.

t: Wöhler and Liebig discover and explain isomers
c: 1825 – Friedrich Wöhler and Justus von Liebig perform the first confirmed discovery and explanation of isomers, earlier named by Berzelius.

t: Prout classifies biomolecules into modern groups
c: 1827 – William Prout classifies biomolecules into their modern groupings: carbohydrates, proteins and lipids.

t: Wöhler synthesizes urea, disproving vitalism
c: 1828 – Friedrich Wöhler synthesizes urea, thereby establishing that organic compounds could be produced from inorganic starting materials, disproving the…

t: Wöhler and Liebig discover functional groups
c: 1832 – Friedrich Wöhler and Justus von Liebig discover and explain functional groups and radicals in relation to organic chemistry.

t: Hess proposes Hess's law
c: 1840 – Germain Hess proposes Hess's law, an early statement of the law of conservation of energy, which establishes that energy changes in a chemical process…

t: Kolbe obtains acetic acid from inorganic sources
c: 1847 – Hermann Kolbe obtains acetic acid from completely inorganic sources, further disproving vitalism.

t: Lord Kelvin establishes absolute zero concept
c: 1848 – Lord Kelvin establishes concept of absolute zero, the temperature at which all molecular motion ceases.

t: Pasteur clarifies optical rotation in tartaric acid

t: Beer proposes Beer's law
c: 1852 – August Beer proposes Beer's law, which explains the relationship between the composition of a mixture and the amount of light it will absorb.

t: Silliman pioneers petroleum cracking methods
c: 1855 – Benjamin Silliman, Jr. pioneers methods of petroleum cracking, which makes the entire modern petrochemical industry possible.

t: Kekulé proposes carbon is tetravalent
c: 1857 – Friedrich August Kekulé von Stradonitz proposes that carbon is tetravalent, or forms exactly four chemical bonds.

t: Kirchhoff and Bunsen establish spectroscopy
c: 1859–1860 – Gustav Kirchhoff and Robert Bunsen lay the foundations of spectroscopy as a means of chemical analysis, which lead them to the discovery of caesium…

t: Cannizzaro compiles atomic weights table

t: Parkes exhibits Parkesine synthetic polymer
c: 1862 – Alexander Parkes exhibits Parkesine, one of the earliest synthetic polymers, at the International Exhibition in London.

t: Béguyer de Chancourtois publishes telluric helix
c: 1862 – Alexandre-Emile Béguyer de Chancourtois publishes the telluric helix, an early, three-dimensional version of the periodic table of the elements.

t: Newlands proposes law of octaves
c: 1864 – John Newlands proposes the law of octaves, a precursor to the periodic law.

t: Meyer develops early periodic table
c: 1864 – Lothar Meyer develops an early version of the periodic table, with 28 elements organized by valence.

t: Guldberg and Waage propose law of mass action
c: 1864 – Cato Maximilian Guldberg and Peter Waage, building on Claude Louis Berthollet's ideas, proposed the law of mass action.

t: Loschmidt determines Avogadro constant
c: 1865 – Johann Josef Loschmidt determines exact number of molecules in a mole, later named Avogadro constant.

t: Kekulé establishes benzene ring structure

t: Van 't Hoff and Le Bel explain molecular chirality

t: Gibbs publishes work on thermodynamics

t: Boltzmann establishes statistical chemistry foundations
c: 1877 – Ludwig Boltzmann establishes statistical derivations of many important physical and chemical concepts, including entropy, and distributions of molecular…

t: Arrhenius develops ion theory
c: 1883 – Svante Arrhenius develops ion theory to explain conductivity in electrolytes.

t: Van 't Hoff publishes chemical kinetics study
c: 1884 – Jacobus Henricus van 't Hoff publishes Études de Dynamique chimique, a seminal study on chemical kinetics.

t: Fischer proposes structure of purine
c: 1884 – Hermann Emil Fischer proposes structure of purine, a key structure in many biomolecules, which he later synthesized in 1898.

t: Le Chatelier develops chemical equilibrium principle
c: 1884 – Henry Louis Le Chatelier develops Le Chatelier's principle, which explains the response of dynamic chemical equilibria to external stresses.

t: Eugen Goldstein names cathode and canal rays
c: 1885 – Eugen Goldstein names the cathode ray, later discovered to be composed of electrons, and the canal ray, later discovered to be positive hydrogen ions…

t: Alfred Werner discovers octahedral cobalt complex structure
c: 1893 – Alfred Werner discovers the octahedral structure of cobalt complexes, thus establishing the field of coordination chemistry.

t: William Ramsay discovers the noble gases
c: 1894–1898 – William Ramsay discovers the noble gases, which fill a large and unexpected gap in the periodic table and led to models of chemical bonding.

t: J. J. Thomson discovers the electron

t: Maria and Pierre Curie isolate radium and polonium
c: 1898 – Maria Sklodowska-Curie and Pierre Curie isolate radium and polonium from pitchblende.

t: Ernest Rutherford discovers radioactivity source in decaying atoms
Mikhail Tsvet invents chromatography
c: 1903 – Mikhail Semyonovich Tsvet invents chromatography, an important analytic technique.

t: Hantaro Nagaoka proposes early nuclear atomic model
c: 1904 – Hantaro Nagaoka proposes an early nuclear model of the atom, where electrons orbit a dense massive nucleus.

t: Fritz Haber and Carl Bosch develop ammonia synthesis

t: Albert Einstein explains Brownian motion and atomic theory
c: 1905 – Albert Einstein explains Brownian motion in a way that definitively proves atomic theory.

t: Leo Baekeland invents bakelite plastic
c: 1907 – Leo Hendrik Baekeland invents bakelite, one of the first commercially successful plastics.

t: S. P. L. Sørensen invents the pH concept

t: First Solvay Conference held in Brussels
c: 1911 – The first Solvay Conference is held in Brussels, bringing together most of the most prominent scientists of the day.

t: Ernest Rutherford, Hans Geiger

t: William Braggs propose Bragg's law and X-ray crystallography

t: Peter Debye develops molecular dipole concept
c: 1912 – Peter Debye develops the concept of molecular dipole to describe asymmetric charge distribution in some molecules.

t: Henry Moseley introduces atomic number concept

t: Frederick Soddy proposes concept of isotopes
c: 1913 – Frederick Soddy proposes the concept of isotopes, that elements with the same chemical properties may have differing atomic weights.

t: J. J. Thomson develops mass spectrometry technique
Otto Stern and Walther Gerlach establish quantum spin
c: 1921 – Otto Stern and Walther Gerlach establish concept of quantum mechanical spin in subatomic particles.

c: 1923 – Gilbert N.

t: Gilbert Lewis develops electron pair acid-base theory
c: 1923 – Gilbert N.

t: Louis de Broglie introduces wave model of atoms
c: 1924 – Louis de Broglie introduces the wave-model of atomic structure, based on the ideas of wave–particle duality.

t: Wolfgang Pauli develops the exclusion principle
c: 1925 – Wolfgang Pauli develops the exclusion principle, which states that no two electrons around a single nucleus may have the same quantum state, as…

t: Erwin Schrödinger proposes the Schrödinger equation
c: 1925 – Erwin Schrödinger proposes the Schrödinger equation, which provides a mathematical basis for the wave model of atomic structure.

t: Werner Heisenberg develops the uncertainty principle
c: 1927 – Werner Heisenberg develops the uncertainty principle which, among other things, explains the mechanics of electron motion around the nucleus.

t: London and Heitler explain covalent bonding quantum mechanically

t: Linus Pauling publishes Pauling's rules
c: 1929 – Linus Pauling publishes Pauling's rules, which are key principles for the use of X-ray crystallography to deduce molecular structure.

t: Erich Hückel proposes Hückel's rule
c: 1931 – Erich Hückel proposes Hückel's rule, which explains when a planar ring molecule will have aromatic properties.

t: Harold Urey discovers deuterium
c: 1931 – Harold Urey discovers deuterium by fractionally distilling liquid hydrogen.

t: James Chadwick discovers the neutron
c: 1932 – James Chadwick discovers the neutron.

t: Pauling and Mulliken quantify electronegativity
c: 1932–1934 – Linus Pauling and Robert Mulliken quantify electronegativity, devising the scales that now bear their names.

t: Wallace Carothers and DuPont invent nylon
c: 1935 – Wallace Carothers leads a team of chemists at DuPont who invent nylon, one of the most commercially successful synthetic polymers in history.

t: Eugene Houdry develops catalytic cracking method
c: 1937 – Eugene Houdry develops a method of industrial scale catalytic cracking of petroleum, leading to the development of the first modern oil refinery.

t: Kapitsa, Allen, and Misener produce superfluid helium-4

t: Hahn and Meitner discover nuclear fission
c: 1939 – Otto Hahn and Lise Meitner discover the process of nuclear fission in uranium.

t: Pauling publishes The Nature of the Chemical Bond
c: 1939 – Linus Pauling publishes The Nature of the Chemical Bond, a compilation of a decades worth of work on chemical bonding.

t: McMillan and Abelson identify neptunium
c: 1940 – Edwin McMillan and Philip H.

t: Glenn Seaborg creates new atomic nuclei
c: 1941 – Glenn T.

t: Woodward and Doering synthesize quinine
c: 1944 – Robert Burns Woodward and William von Eggers Doering successfully synthesized of quinine.

Pauling deduces protein secondary structure

t: Woodward, Wilkinson, and Fischer discover ferrocene

t: Watson and Crick propose DNA structure
c: 1953 – James D.

t: Jens Skou discovers Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase enzyme
c: 1957 – Jens Skou discovers Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase, the first ion-transporting enzyme.

t: Perutz and Kendrew elucidate myoglobin structure
c: 1958 – Max Perutz and John Kendrew use X-ray crystallography to elucidate a protein structure, specifically sperm whale myoglobin.

t: Neil Bartlett synthesizes xenon hexafluoroplatinate
c: 1962 – Neil Bartlett synthesizes xenon hexafluoroplatinate, showing for the first time that the noble gases can form chemical compounds.
